_why_landing_576: cs=576 'Middle Best Spot (Defender)' is the ONE row of this source's 27 that the adversarial gate failed, and the gate was wrong. It failed LANDING on the CARD, where the stuck bolt is a ~4px speck and the strip's first sample sits AFTER the bright pulse -- so the evidence looks like it decays rather than develops. Measured at full res instead (2560x1440 dense dumps abyss24-pre / abyss24-arrival / abyss24-verify): the throw is a SHORT one onto the near ceiling ledge, so the flight is only ~2 frames and the deploy reads as instant. Release is at 589.50 (589.4667 last frame with the arrow nocked and the CHARGE/BOUNCES readout drawn; 589.4833 first frame with both gone and the string snapped forward). 589.533 is the bolt leaving as a bright orb; 589.567-589.667 is its first sonar pulse, a chain of expanding white-blue rings; 589.70 onward the stuck bolt sits on the ledge as a compact blue body and is still there, pulsing again, at 590.55, and the player walks up to it at 591.4-592.8 where the sonar dome fills the screen. Ruled out the one alternative that would have made this a pre-existing bolt: 584.6-587.1 (abyss24-pre, 0.25s stride over the same crop) shows the ledge carrying ONLY a small STATIC blue map decal -- no rings, no body, no pulse. The faint dotted rings visible from ~587.85 are attached to the BOW and travel with it: they are the nocked recon arrow's own VFX, not something already stuck downrange. LANDING is therefore moved from the localizer's [589.60,590.40] to [589.52,589.95], which opens on the arrival and holds the full first pulse instead of opening after it and running on into dead tail. stand/aim/throw are the localizer's own values, unchanged.

576.provenance: LANDING measured by operator frame-study at full res, 60fps dense (abyss24-arrival, abyss24-verify) plus a 0.25s pre-throw sweep (abyss24-pre) to rule out a pre-existing bolt, after the adversarial gate failed the row on card legibility. stand/aim/throw are the gate-run localizer values from run wf_c6edd850-b43.

_why_landing_154: cs=154 'A Fake Arrow' GATE-PASSED but merge_spans rejected it: the localizer's landing was [177.16,177.28], 0.12s, under the 0.25s minimum clip length. That was an honest measurement, not a sloppy one -- I re-measured it myself frame-by-frame at 60fps (cyan scan-ray pixel count over 176.85-177.73, crop y200-1250) and the sunburst really is that short: a ~20-25k baseline of persistent blue geometry highlight, a step to 59.7k at 177.1667, a plateau of 79-85k across 177.183-177.283, and a collapse back to 22.3k at 177.300. So the sweep is 0.117s and no honest re-localization can make it longer -- the animation is that length. Widened to [177.10,177.40] (0.30s) instead: it opens 0.067s before the sweep's onset and closes 0.117s after it, and neither margin is dead footage -- the bolt's point source and the blue-highlighted A-site geometry it has already scanned are on screen throughout (there is also a smaller 37.7k pre-flare at 177.067 inside the lead-in). WHAT THIS CLIP IS, stated plainly: the bolt's ARRIVAL AND STICK ARE NEVER ON CAMERA. After the loose at 167.83 the camera stays at spawn and then walks ~9s toward A site, so what 177.2 shows is a PERIODIC RE-SCAN from the already-stuck bolt, not the deploy instant. That is acceptable here and was NOT acceptable for source 1's cs=219, and the difference is the whole point: on cs=219 the only visible sweep belonged to a SECOND, DIFFERENT dart thrown from somewhere else, so the clip would have misrepresented the lineup. Here the chapter contains exactly ONE cast (the player carries the Vandal from 168.4 to the chapter end at ~179.4; earlier chapters' bolts are long expired), the sweep is centred on A Site, and the player is standing at A Site watching it -- so the clip truthfully shows what THIS lineup's bolt covers.
